applies_why: Yes: the judge text resolves a chain-vs-chain collision (D6 vs C1) by assessing the challenger's seed/loins chain and the defender's chain, so K-C governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrases 'never verse by verse' and 'does not name Joseph as the begetter': I weighed whether the judge was merely assessing footing or using a forbidden verse-level requirement that the chain explicitly name Joseph; I read it as the latter.
why: The judge discounts a footed chain because it does not explicitly name Joseph, which is the retired stating-verse test rather than chain-vs-chain footing.
